record.paper_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
record.original_question: For cross-silo federated learning, what formal privacy notion should be optimized in realistic deployments, especially when other participating silos may be a more important threat than the outside world and when each silo may represent many end users whose privacy may need to be protected at the user level?

evidence.quote: On the other hand, for a practically persuasive claim, we would usually need a notion of local differential privacy, as the potential threat from other clients is likely to be more important. In cases when the clients are not considered a signiﬁcant threat, each client could control the data from a number of their respective users, and a formal privacy guarantee might be needed on such user-level basis. Depending on application, other objectives could be worth pursuing. This area has not been systematically explored.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a cross-silo federated learning setting in which a finite collection of silos (institutions) S_1, ..., S_K jointly train a model by exchanging messages with a coordinator (or with each other) according to some protocol M. Each silo S_k holds a private dataset D_k = {x_{k,1}, ..., x_{k,n_k}} corresponding to n_k distinct end users. Two threat models are of particular interest:

(a) Inter-silo threat: other participating silos S_j (j ≠ k) are considered potential adversaries who observe all messages sent by S_k during the protocol and may collude.

(b) User-level threat: an adversary (which may include other silos and/or the coordinator) attempts to infer information about an individual end user whose data may comprise an arbitrary subset of records within a single silo, rather than a single record.

Recall the standard definitions:
• A randomized mechanism M is (ε, δ)-centrally differentially private if for all neighboring datasets D, D' differing in one record and all measurable sets E, Pr[M(D) ∈ E] ≤ e^ε Pr[M(D') ∈ E] + δ.
• M is (ε, δ)-locally differentially private if each user's data is randomized before release, i.e. for all x, x' and measurable E, Pr[M(x) ∈ E] ≤ e^ε Pr[M(x') ∈ E] + δ.
• User-level differential privacy strengthens the neighboring relation so that D and D' differ in the entire collection of records belonging to a single user.

Problem. Formulate and justify a formal privacy notion P (together with its quantitative parameters) for cross-silo federated learning that simultaneously:
   1. provides a meaningful guarantee against an adversary consisting of an arbitrary coalition of the other K−1 silos (and possibly the coordinator),
   2. provides a guarantee at the user level when each silo holds data from many end users (so that all records contributed by any single user are protected as a group), and
   3. is achievable by a concrete protocol M with utility (e.g., excess empirical or population risk for a learning task) comparable, up to explicit factors depending on K, n_k, ε, δ, to the best known bounds under standard central differential privacy.

Provide the definition of P, prove its composition and post-processing properties, exhibit a protocol achieving P with quantified utility, and prove matching or near-matching lower bounds showing the privacy/utility trade-off is essentially tight. Systematically compare P to local, central, shuffle, and distributed differential privacy in the cross-silo setting.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of which formal privacy notion is best suited for cross-silo federated learning—balancing inter-silo threats and user-level protection—remains an active area of research. Subsequent works have proposed candidate notions such as inter-silo record-level DP, silo-specific sample-level privacy, hierarchical/user-level DP, and shuffle/distributed DP variants, but no consensus or fully systematic theory has emerged. The area is widely described as still open.

status_evidence.title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
status_evidence.snippet: Identifies cross-silo privacy notions as not systematically explored.
status_evidence.claim: The original survey lists this as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Differentially Private Federated Learning: A Systematic Review
status_evidence.snippet: Recent surveys note that cross-silo DP definitions (ISRL-DP, user-level DP, silo-level DP) are still under active investigation with no unified framework.
status_evidence.claim: Active research, no consensus notion has been adopted.

status_evidence.title: Cross-Silo Federated Learning with Record-Level Personalized Differential Privacy
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes inter-silo record-level DP variants, indicating ongoing development of suitable notions.
status_evidence.claim: Multiple competing notions are being proposed; the question is not settled.
